summary:
Investors are rushing to buy insurance against potential defaults among the companies financing artificial intelligence infrastructure. Weekly trading volumes of credit default swaps (CDS) tied to Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Nvidia, Broadcom, Oracle and SpaceX rose to $9.5 billion, more than four times the volume recorded in July. Insurance costs have reached distressed levels for AI infrastructure provider CoreWeave, where 5-year spreads hit a record 1,090 basis points, while Meta and Nvidia saw spreads hit 108 and 101 basis points respectively.

AI-related debt issuance for chips and data centers reached approximately $466 billion in 2026, up from $101 billion during the same period in 2025. Oracle's insurance costs more than doubled since January and were trading at 350 basis points as of Oct. 20. Market participants are utilizing these derivatives to hedge against rising corporate leverage and uncertain returns on capital expenditures within the sector.

AI DEBT FEARS are triggering a surge in demand for protection against corporate debt defaults:

Weekly trading volumes of credit default swaps (CDS) linked to Oracle, $ORCL, SpaceX, $SPCX, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Broadcom, and Nvidia, $NVDA, surged to a record $9.5 billion.

This is more than QUADRUPLE the volume recorded in July.

This comes as AI-related debt issuance has skyrocketed to ~$466 billion in 2026, up from $101 billion over the same period in 2025, as companies finance massive investments in data centers and chips.

In effect, 5-year CDS spreads, or the cost of insuring against default, spiked to 108 basis points for Meta and 101 bps for Nvidia, while Oracle's more than doubled to 322 bps since January.

The surge is even more pronounced among highly leveraged AI infrastructure providers, with CoreWeave's CDS exploding to a record 1,090 bps, deep into distressed territory.

Investors are increasingly using these derivatives to hedge against a potential downturn in AI stocks and debt, amid concerns over rising leverage, uncertain returns on infrastructure spending, and the sector's circular financing.

Investors are rushing to hedge against an AI-driven market crash.
